summary.text: Cory Booker is the incumbent Democratic U.S. Senator from New Jersey, in office since October 2013. A Stanford, Oxford and Yale Law graduate, he started a legal-services nonprofit in Newark, served on the Newark City Council (1998-2002) and as Mayor of Newark (2006-2013), and ran for the 2020 Democratic presidential nomination. He ran unopposed in the 2026 Democratic primary and chairs the Senate Democrats' Strategic Communications Committee.

paragraphs.text: Born in Washington, D.C., in 1969 and grew up in northern New Jersey.

Earned a bachelor's degree in political science (1991) and a master's in sociology (1992) from Stanford University, where he played varsity football; as a Rhodes Scholar, earned a graduate degree in history at the University of Oxford (1994), and received a J.D. from Yale Law School in 1997.

After law school he moved to Newark and, according to his Senate biography, started a nonprofit providing legal services to low-income families; he also worked as a staff attorney at the Urban Justice Center and as program coordinator of the Newark Youth Project.
Elected to the Newark City Council at 29 and served from 1998 to 2002; served as Mayor of Newark from 2006 to 2013.
Won a special election to the U.S. Senate in October 2013, was re-elected to a full term in 2014 and re-elected in 2020.
Announced a campaign for the 2020 Democratic presidential nomination on February 1, 2019, and suspended it on January 13, 2020.

Serves on the Senate Judiciary, Foreign Relations, Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry, and Small Business committees; elected chairman of the Senate Democrats' Strategic Communications Committee without opposition on December 3, 2024.

His Senate biography cites his work on the First Step Act, a criminal justice law enacted in December 2018. On March 31, 2025, he began a Senate floor speech that lasted 25 hours and five minutes, the longest in Senate history.
According to his Senate biography, he lives in Newark's Central Ward.
